title: Medarbejder til økonomiafdelingen (2-10 stillinger)
description:
Medarbejder til økonomiafdelingen (2-10 stillinger)

 I vores økonomiafdeling har vi en stor og vigtig opgave foran os. Vi har en del bilag og data, der har hobet sig op over en længere periode, som skal scannes, bogføres og struktureres. Da det er en omfattende opgave, søger vi et team på 2-10 medarbejdere, som kan arbejde tæt sammen, sparre med hinanden og løbende afløse hinanden i ferier og eksamensperioder.

Du vil blive en central del af teamet og få solid hands-on erfaring med klassiske regnskabsopgaver. Du behøver ikke at have erfaring i forvejen – vi sørger for en grundig oplæring i alle vores systemer, så du bliver klædt ordentligt på til opgaven. Der kan også være ad hoc opgaver som der ikke er beskrevet i opslaget.

 

Dine primære arbejdsopgaver:

·       Oprydning og digitalisering: Scanning af fysiske bilag/kvitteringer og organisering af historisk materiale. Vi skal nok hjælpe dig med det.

·       Bogføring og kontrol: Kontering af omkostninger og medarbejderudlæg i e-conomic og Pleo. Vi skal nok hjælpe dig med det.

·       Data- og systemarbejde: Indtastnings- og afstemningsarbejde i Excel og Dataløn. Vi skal nok hjælpe dig med det.

·       Regnskab, fakturering og styring: Løbende assistance med debitor-/kreditorstyring, fakturering, fakturabehandling samt hjælp ved månedsafslutning. Vi skal nok hjælpe dig med det.

·       Analyse og Excel/Libre: Ad hoc-opgaver inden for Excel-modellering. Vi skal nok hjælpe dig med det.

·       Ad hoc-assistance: Koordinering via Outlook samt hjælp til praktisk planlægning og afholdelse af interne møder og træningssessioner. Vi skal nok hjælpe dig med det.

·       Kommunikation: Formidling af virksomhedens interne regler og retningslinjer for udlæg og bilagshåndtering til resten af husets medarbejdere. Vi skal nok hjælpe dig med det.

 

Hvem er du?….måske

·       Du kan også være gang i et sabbatår.

·       Du kan også være ledig.

·       Du trives med rutineopgaver og motiveres af at få en stor oprydningsopgave i mål i fællesskab med dit team.

·       Du har mod på at lære systemer som e-conomic, Pleo, Dataløn og Outlook at kende (eller kender dem allerede).

·       Du arbejder struktureret, har et skarpt øje for detaljer og er en god holdspiller.

·       Du er serviceminded og har mod på at guide kolleger i organisationen omkring vores finansielle retningslinjer.

 

Hvad tilbyder vi?

·       Høj fleksibilitet: Vi tilpasser arbejdstiden efter dit studie eller efter dit behov, så der altid er plads til eksamensperioder og forelæsninger.

·       Grundig oplæring – vi forventer ikke, at du kan det hele på forhånd.

·       Stærk erfaring på dit CV med udbredte og markedskendte systemer (Pleo, e-conomic, Dataløn).

·       En uformel arbejdsplads med et stærkt sammenhold i det nye team.

·       Timer: deltid eller fuldtid – det er op til dig

 

Arbejdssted: Skibby (4050 Frederikssund, Frederikssund Kommune / Region Hovedstaden)
Opstart: Hurtigst muligt.

 

 Ansøgning

Vi vil gerne vide, hvem du er – også ud over det, der står på dit CV. Send os derfor et meget, meget kort personlig ansøgning mærket:”studentermedhjælper”, der giver os et indtryk af dit potentiale og din personlighed. Du bestemmer helt selv formen, og du må meget gerne være kreativ!

Vedlæg dit CV samt din kreative ansøgning, og send det hele til josiah@curam.dk hurtigst muligt.

Vi tager løbende samtaler, så tøv ikke med at sende din ansøgning!

Har du spørgsmål til stillingen, er du velkommen til at kontakte Josiah – Økonomiansvarlig på josiah@curam.dk.

Finance Department Staff (2–10 positions)

 

Our finance department faces a major and important task. A significant volume of vouchers, documents and data has accumulated over a long period and needs to be scanned, recorded, and organized. As this is a substantial undertaking, we are looking for a team of 2–10 employees who can work closely together, collaborate, and cover for one another during holidays and exam periods.

You will become a key part of the team and gain solid hands-on experience with standard accounting tasks. Prior experience is not required—we provide thorough training in all our systems to ensure you are well-prepared for the job. There may also be ad hoc tasks not specifically listed in this job posting.

 

Your primary tasks:

• Organization and digitization: Scanning physical vouchers/receipts and organizing historical records. We will assist you with this.

• Bookkeeping and verification: Coding expenses and employee reimbursements in e-conomic and Pleo. We will assist you with this.

• Data and system work: Data entry and reconciliation in Excel and Dataløn. We will assist you with this.

• Accounting, invoicing, and management: Ongoing assistance with accounts receivable/payable, invoicing, invoice processing, and month-end closing. We will assist you with this.

• Analysis and Excel/Libre: Ad hoc tasks involving Excel modeling. We will assist you with this.

• Ad hoc assistance: Coordination via Outlook and help with the practical planning and hosting of internal meetings and training sessions. We’ll help you with that.

• Communication: Communicating the company’s internal rules and guidelines regarding expenses and receipt handling to the rest of the staff. We’ll help you with that.

 

Who are you?… perhaps…

• You might be taking a gap year.

• You might be currently unemployed.

• You enjoy routine tasks and are motivated by successfully completing a major cleanup project together with your team.

• You work in a structured manner, have a keen eye for detail, and are a good team player.

• You are service-minded and comfortable guiding colleagues across the organization regarding our financial guidelines.

 

What do we offer?

• High flexibility: We tailor working hours to fit your studies or personal needs, ensuring there is always room for exam periods and lectures.

• Thorough training – we don’t expect you to know everything from day one.

• Valuable experience for your CV working with widely used, market-leading systems (Pleo, e-conomic, Dataløn).

• An informal workplace with a strong sense of team spirit. Location: Skibby (4050 Frederikssund, Frederikssund Municipality / Capital Region of Denmark)

• Hours: partime or full time – its up to you

Start date: As soon as possible.

 

 

Application

We would like to know who you are—beyond just what is on your CV. Please send us a very brief personal application marked "student assistant" that gives us an impression of your potential and personality. You are free to choose the format, and we encourage you to be creative!

Please attach your CV and your creative application, and send everything to josiah@curam.dk as soon as possible.

We are conducting interviews on an ongoing basis, so don't hesitate to send your application!

If you have any questions about the position, you are welcome to contact Josiah (Finance Manager) at josiah@curam.dk.

title: Associate Professor in Radiography
description:
A position as associate professor (10% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Radiology (Odense), the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark.

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology, Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), in collaboration with University College Lillebælt (UCL) and Odense Universitetshospital (OUH), invites applications for a position as Associate Professor in Radiography, with 10% research time at the Department of Radiology, OUH. The position is offered for a five-year period with the possibility of extension. The starting date is subject to agreement.

About the research unit

UNIFY – Research and Innovation Unit of Radiology conducts high-quality research across all radiological specialties and contributes significantly to the education and development of highly qualified staff for both clinical and academic work.

The unit values researchers with diverse professional backgrounds and has approximately 20 affiliated members, including a professor, associate professors, PhD students, adjunct professors and others.

The unit has a well-established research environment and organises a number of regular activities and meetings throughout the year, including research retreats combining academic and social activities.

Research and Teaching Responsibilities
The position involves research, academic development, research training, teaching, including examinations, supervision and assessment activities.

Qualifications and Expectations
The Associate Professor must hold a primary position at UCL.

The successful applicant must have documented research and teaching experience within radiography and a particular interest in ultrasound.

Furthermore, strong collaborative skills are required in order to further develop research in radiography, both across disciplines and at national and international level. Having international research collaborators is considered an advantage but is not a requirement.

Joint Research Strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and OUH

The joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and OUH sets the direction for our shared research activities in the coming years.

Based on the vision, “We conduct research together to create the patient care of the future,” particular emphasis is placed on:

  • Research across disciplines, with people at the centre

  • Strong research environments as a driving force for development

  • The research pathway from idea to impact

Further information about the joint research strategy is available on the SDU website.

Applicants Must Document

  • A PhD degree or equivalent postgraduate research qualifications

  • Relevant research experience documented through publications in international peer-reviewed journals

  • Relevant clinical experience

  • Relevant experience in educational administration

  • A successful track record in obtaining research funding

Applicants must meet the qualifications required at Associate Professor level in accordance with the applicable Danish Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Reporting

The Associate Professor will report to Head of Research Bo Mussmann on matters relating to the associate professorship.

Contact

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Research Bo Mussmann, Department of Clinical Research/OUH: Email: bo.mussmann@rsyd.dk, Telephone: +45 20 59 88 56

Application deadline

01.11.2026 at 23:59 CET

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Associate Professor is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed associate professor allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Kløvervænget 10, 2nd floor, 5000 Odense C, Denmark.  

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below. 

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply. 

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation. 

Your application must include the following as PDF files:

Please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total).

  • a motivation letter 

  • a detailed CV 

  • degree certificates (including a Ph.D.-diploma)

  • a complete and numbered list of publications 

  • 6 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file. 

  • It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file

  • a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

  • a research plan

  • a detailed description of research experience 

  • an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application

Incomplete applications regarding the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

title: Purchaser - Global Supply Chain
description:
Do you have experience with technical or project procurement in a larger international company? Would you like to help develop a global supply chain in an international project-driven organization? Then you may be the Purchaser we are looking for.

We are upgrading, servicing, and operating engine- and biomass-based power plants around the world. This creates a continuous need to source goods and services from subcontractors and ensure reliable transport for our customers.

For our Global Supply Chain department, we are looking for an outgoing and internationally minded colleague with commitment, determination, and a positive attitude. The department consists of 20 employees responsible for procurement, warehousing, and transport of goods and services.

BWSC – Ever better energy! 

Join us in our mission of building a world of sustainable energy and make a meaningful impact on the world of power generation and energy conversion.

BWSC is a leading player in the power generation industry, specializing in the service, operations, and maintenance of power plants. We are seeking to always provide Ever Better Energy whether it comes to optimizing a conventional power plant, operating a biomass power plant or constructing new energy facilities. Our commitment to excellence, innovation, and environmental stewardship sets us apart in the industry.

Your responsibilities

  • Support Project Procurement Managers with procurement tasks related to the execution of upgrading, service- and maintenance projects for engine and biomass power plants globally.
  • Obtain quotations from suppliers and place purchase orders within a defined area of responsibility.
  • Participate in broader departmental activities such as category management, supplier relationship development, negotiations, and implementation of supplier agreements.
  • Contribute to identifying and evaluating potential suppliers.
  • Convert purchase requisitions into purchase orders.
  • Maintain and update various data, including supplier data, in the ERP system.
  • Follow up on purchase orders, deliveries and invoice approvals.
  • Assist with various development-oriented Global Supply Chain tasks within BWSC, including work instructions and new workflows.

The work is carried out in close collaboration with other departments in a dynamic and project-oriented organization. A flexible, cooperative, and positive attitude is therefore essential.

Desired Background and Qualifications

  • Experience within procurement, including purchase order placement and follow-up.
  • Completed education as an office assistant and/or relevant higher education qualification.
  • Minimum 3 years of practical experience with technical or project procurement.
  • Strong written and spoken English skills.
  • Good IT skills and experience with ERP systems, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
  • Ability to work in a structured manner and meet deadlines.

What do we offer? 

At BWSC we build inspiring careers locally and internationally and give you access to a great network of possibilities. 

We offer you a position with great colleagues and the opportunity to bring your skills into play and grow professionally and personally. As a Purchaser at BWSC, you will receive a competitive starting salary and a strong reward package.

We offer an exciting position in a skilled, collaborative, and project-driven work environment, with opportunities for professional development and growth.

We have a good canteen, fitness facilities, and an active Staff Club that organizes various events and activities. Our HQ is located in Allerød, close to the train station and only a 30-minute ride from central Copenhagen.

Ready for a challenge?  

We review applications and invite relevant candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Supply Chain Manager Anders S. A. Pedersen at asap@bwsc.dk.

BWSC is committed to promoting equality and diversity. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age. Therefore, we do not recommend specifying age, etc., in the application. 

BWSC no longer receives or handles applications received via email due to GDPR requirements. In order for your application to be processed, you must submit your application via our online recruitment system. 

Get to know us even better on our website, www.bwsc.com, where you can learn more about our business, organization, project portfolio, and what we want to achieve at BWSC. 

About BWSC 

Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractor A/S (BWSC) is a global power plant Operation & Maintenance and technical service provider with engineering expertise, enabling power plant owners to deliver cleaner and affordable energy. We are experts in servicing, upgrading, operating, and maintaining energy systems for diesel, natural gas, and renewable baseload power plants worldwide. We help our customers increase reliability and availability of energy production, improve efficiency and performance of their power plant, design and integrate future-proof technologies, and secure lower cost of maintenance.

Our people are at the core of everything we do and key to building strong relationships with our customers. We invest in our people and their wellbeing, supporting professional development and creating an environment where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and personal growth drive our continued success and growth as a company.

title: Expression of Interest - Offshore Helicopter Pilots
description:
Join Our Pilot Pool for Future Opportunities

At Avincis, we are proud to support the green energy transition by providing safe and efficient helicopter transport to offshore wind farms and associated installations.

As the offshore wind industry continues to grow, we are preparing for potential future expansion of our operations in Denmark and Northern Germany. We are therefore interested in connecting with experienced helicopter pilots who may wish to join our team as new opportunities arise.

---

Please note that this is not an active vacancy. We are building a network of qualified helicopter pilots who may be interested in future opportunities within our operations. Candidates whose qualifications and experience match our requirements may be contacted as suitable positions become available.

About the Opportunity

Pilots joining Avincis operate Airbus H135 and H145 helicopters in support of offshore wind operations, including:

  • Personnel transport to offshore wind farms and vessels

  • Crew change operations

  • Equipment transport

  • Offshore hoist operations

  • IFR and offshore flight operations

Our current Danish bases include Esbjerg, Roskilde, Grenaa and Thorsminde, supporting some of Northern Europe's largest offshore wind projects.

While no positions are currently guaranteed, candidates meeting our requirements may be contacted regarding future opportunities as business needs develop.

Who We Are Looking For

Minimum Qualifications

title: Consultant Interventional Cardiologist
description:
Consultant Interventional Cardiologist – PCI On-Call Service

Department of Cardiology, Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark

The opportunity
Are you an experienced interventional cardiologist looking to join a highly specialised university hospital with a strong clinical, academic and collaborative environment?

The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is seeking one or more Consultant Interventional Cardiologists from the EU/EØS to join our team. We welcome applications from candidates who are already qualified to participate in a PCI on-call service, as well as experienced PCI operators who are motivated to develop the additional competencies required for on-call duties.

The position is available as soon as possible or by mutual agreement.

This is an opportunity to work in a busy interventional cardiology environment, contribute to the development of specialised cardiac care and collaborate with highly skilled colleagues across cardiology, cardiac surgery and other disciplines.

The position
Your primary clinical responsibilities will be within interventional cardiology, particularly percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
The position includes participation in the department's PCI on-call service.

You will be part of a multidisciplinary team providing specialised care for patients with ischaemic heart disease, including patients requiring urgent and complex coronary interventions.
Depending on your experience, qualifications and the department's clinical needs, there may also be opportunities to contribute to the development of other specialised interventional services, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and chronic total occlusion (CTO) procedures.

Alongside your clinical responsibilities, you will contribute to the department's research, teaching and professional development activities, as well as relevant administrative and organisational tasks.

What we offer
  • The opportunity to work in a busy university hospital with an established PCI service and a broad range of specialised cardiology services.
  • Professional development: Opportunities to further develop your interventional skills and, where appropriate, expand your expertise into complex PCI, TAVI or CTO procedures.
  • A strong multidisciplinary team: Close collaboration with cardiologists across subspecialties, cardiothoracic anaesthetists and cardiac surgeons.
  • An academic environment: Opportunities to participate in clinical research, teaching and the development of new treatment pathways.
  • Supportive colleagues and leadership: We value professional respect, constructive collaboration and a positive working environment.
  • Flexible working arrangements: Working hours and duty schedules are organised within the applicable employment framework.
  • An international perspective: The opportunity to join a university hospital committed to clinical excellence, research, education and continuous improvement.

Qualifications and experience
Essential requirements
  • You hold specialist certification in cardiology.
  • You have or are able to obtain a Danish Authorization to practice medicine
  • You are fluent in or command a professional working proficiency in Danish. Norwegian or Swedish (B2/C1 level)
  • Or are willing to learn Danish
  • You can perform PCI procedures independently.
  • You have the clinical judgement and professional skills required to manage patients with ischaemic heart disease.
  • You communicate effectively and work constructively with colleagues across clinical disciplines.
  • You can maintain an overview and make sound clinical decisions in a demanding and sometimes unpredictable environment.
  • You are committed to high standards of patient care, patient safety and continuous professional development.
  • You are willing to contribute to the department's clinical, organisational and educational activities and to take on the leadership and supervisory responsibilities associated with a consultant position.

Desirable qualifications
  • Experience participating in a PCI on-call service.
  • Experience from a university hospital or another highly specialised cardiac centre.
  • Experience in complex PCI, TAVI or CTO procedures.
  • A PhD, or other research qualifications or a strong record of scientific publications.
  • Experience in clinical research, teaching or quality improvement.
  • Experience in a PCI on-call service is an advantage but is not essential, provided you are an independent PCI operator and are motivated to acquire the necessary competencies following an appropriate period of training and induction.

About the Department
The Department of Cardiology at Aalborg University Hospital is a large, specialised and research-active department providing advanced care across a broad range of cardiovascular conditions, including ischaemic heart disease, cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, valvular heart disease, thoracic aortic aneurysms, pericardial diseases, thromboembolic disorders and dyslipidaemia.

Our department performs approximately:
  • 6,000 invasive procedures annually
  • 8,000 inpatient admissions annually
  • More than 30,000 outpatient consultations annually
  • Approximately 14,000 echocardiographic examinations annually

Our medical team comprises doctors at different stages of postgraduate training and 32 consultant cardiologists, including two professors.
We provide inpatient and outpatient services, operate a cardiac catheterisation laboratory and maintain a dedicated cardiology research unit.
Our work is guided by a shared commitment to clinical excellence, patient safety and involving patients and their families in shared decision-making. We also have a strong responsibility for undergraduate medical education and postgraduate specialist training.
The department operates across three hospital sites in Aalborg, Thisted and Hobro, with the vast majority of clinical activity based at the newly built Aalborg University Hospital.

Salary and terms of employment
This is a full-time position. Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the applicable Danish collective agreement.
The position includes participation in the department's PCI on-call service.
Further details regarding the on-call arrangement and employment conditions can be discussed with the Head of Department or Lead Senior Physician Bent Raungaard tlf. 27201096, e-mail: b.raungaard@rn.dk
 
Application
Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and interviews will be arranged continuously. The advertisement will be withdrawn once the position has been filled.

Ljubica Vukelic Andersen
Head of Department of Cardiology
Aalborg University Hospital, Denmark

Telephone: +45 30 38 25 10

title: Postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception
description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception. The position is available for up to 36 months and is part of a project led by Dr. Gregory Scott Francis that is supported by the SDU Department of Psychology. The starting date is March 15, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Research environment

The postdoc will be affiliated with the Research Unit of Health and Cognitive Psychology. The position is at the SDU Esbjerg campus but will also involve interaction with staff at the SDU Odense campus. 

Project description

A basic process of the visual system is to monitor the location and characteristics of objects in a scene, and the multiple object tracking (MOT) paradigm has identified many fundamental aspects of this process. With a rich literature of empirical results, this paradigm is ready for theoretical development, which this project intends to pursue using an integrate-and-fire neural network model known as LAMINART. A key aspect of the model is the ability to select/segment visual objects, which may explain how people can (seemingly) effortlessly track multiple objects in a dynamic visual scene. 

The successful candidate will be required to design, program and analyze an integrate-and-fire neural network model of visual perception. Good programming (Python) skills are required along with a good understanding of empirical methods and ways to connect empirical findings with model behavior. The position also involves teaching duties.

The project involves collaboration with Prof. Søren Krogh Andersen, also at SDU.

Qualifications

Ideally, applicants for the position should satisfy the following requirements:

  • PhD level in psychology, cognitive (neuro)science, vision science, or a related field

  • Research experience as evidenced by conference contributions and peer-reviewed journal articles in a field related to the offered position

  • Expertise in visual attention and perception

  • Strong analytical skills, including the ability to design, implement, and analyze complex experiments

  • Be willing and able to teach for the Department of Psychology

  • Prior experience with neural network modeling is a plus

  • Prior experience with cognitive modelling is a plus

  • Good command of statistics

  • Good command of Python (or similar programming languages and a willingness to learn)

  • Very good command of the English language in spoken and written form

  • Some knowledge of the Danish language is a plus

Candidates who are about to obtain these qualifications are also encouraged to apply. 

Contact information

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Greg Francis, SDU (email: gfrancis@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 16 98), or Professor Søren Krogh Andersen (email: skandersen@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 49 57)

Salary and terms of employment

The base salary for a postdoctoral researcher is DKK 36,877.42, with an additional job structure supplement of DKK 5,230.75. This brings the total monthly salary to DKK 42,108.16.

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

title: Senior Security Consultant – Incident Response
description:
Do you want to be on the frontline when serious cyber incidents hit? You will lead complex investigations, guide customers through crises, and help shape our incident response services. You will join a highly skilled, collaborative team working with some of the most interesting and challenging cyber cases in the market. 

 

Make a real impact in high‑stakes incidents 

You will be part of a small, expert Incident Response team handling everything from ransomware to targeted attacks across large, complex environments. You will work closely with customers, helping them stay calm, informed and in control during critical situations. You will collaborate with specialists across MDR, Intelligence and Consulting, learn from unique cases, and contribute to the development of tools, methodologies and publications. At CSIS, we invest in your growth with dedicated training time, certifications, and peer learning - in an open, diverse and friendly culture built on “We commit, We care, We succeed together.” 

When you join CSIS, you will get an interesting job in a company and an industry which is growing. You will get interesting challenges, that truly make a difference for our customers, and you will be able to take ownership for your work from start to finish. And you will not least get 130+ fantastic colleagues from all over the world. Besides that, you will get: 

  • Flexible work from home arrangements 

  • A competitive salary and personal benefit package 

  • 5 weeks holiday, plus 5 extra days off each year

  • Healthy, varied lunches (incl. vegetarian and allergy options) 

  • Home-baked goods, healthy snacks, coffee, tea and sodas in the office

Your new job 

In this client-facing role, you will lead major incident response engagements, support multiple customers, guide junior responders, and help clients strengthen their detection and response capabilities. You will work across diverse environments, industries, and technologies, making adaptability and strong communication essential.  

Your responsibilities will be: 

  • Incident Response & Investigations (Client-Facing) 

  • Lead complex and high-severity incident response engagements for customers across varied infrastructures (on-prem, cloud, hybrid). 

  • Perform advanced forensic analysis across a variety of data sources (disk, memory, network, malware, cloud) and provide clients with clear, actionable findings. 

  • Coordinate response activities with client technical teams, management, and legal/compliance contacts. 

  • Develop accurate incident timelines, attribution assessments (where possible), and root-cause analyses. 

  • Customer Communication & Advisory 

  • Act as a trusted advisor to clients during and after incidents, providing guidance on containment, recovery, and long-term improvements. 

  • Deliver polished, professional technical reports and executive summaries for clients. 

  • Present findings to technical teams as well as to senior leadership and non-technical stakeholders. 

  • Preparedness, Consulting & Continuous Improvement 

  • Assist clients with incident readiness assessments, IR playbook creation, tabletop exercises, and contribute to CSIS’s MDR detection engineering. 

  • Contribute to development of internal incident response methodologies, tooling, and best practices. 

  • Mentor and guide junior team members during engagements and internal training. 

 

About you 

You are an experienced incident responder who remains calm and structured under pressure. You enjoy working closely with customers, translating complex technical issues into clear business language, and you value collaboration and knowledge sharing. You are curious, proactive and driven by making a real difference in the fight against cybercrime. 

You bring most of the following: 

Qualifications & Technical Expertise 

  • Hands-on incident response experience, ideally in a consultancy, MSSP, DFIR, or CSIRT environment. 

  • Proven track record leading multi-client or multi-environment incident investigations.

  • Strong knowledge of network protocols and security 

  • Strong experience with SIEM and EDR tools, including detection logic, log correlation, and threat analysis. Hands-on experience with Sentinel/Defender and CrowdStrike a plus. 

  • Advanced digital forensics experience (memory, disk, log, network). 

  • Familiarity with evidence handling, chain-of-custody standards, and forensic reporting. 

  • Strong understanding of attack techniques and threat actor behaviours (MITRE ATT&CK). 

  • Experience in cloud investigations (Azure/AWS/GCP logs, identity, telemetry). 

 

Consultancy-Specific Requirements

  • Excellent client-facing communication: confident, calm, and credible during crises. 

  • Strong written documentation skills for both highly technical and non-technical readers. 

  • Ability to scope engagements, set expectations, and represent the company professionally. 

 

Regulatory & Governance Knowledge

Preferred Skills

Relevant Certifications

Personal Competencies

  • Ability to remain composed and decisive under pressure.

  • Curiosity and passion for threat research, attacker behaviour, and continuous learning. 

 

This is a 24/7/365 function — flexibility, out-of-hours work, on-call coverage and occasional travel is required. 

 

Other conditions

title: Postdoc in environmental medicine
description:
The translational pharmacology research group at Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine (CPPEM), Department of Public Health, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark, invites applications for a fully funded 18 months postdoctoral position. The position is to be filled from January 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.


About the Research Environment

The research areas of CPPEM span from pharmacoepidemiology to clinical studies, and cell-based basic pharmacology and environmental medicine. Collectively, CPPEM has a strong background in exposure to environmental chemicals, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacogenetics, pharmacokinetics, drug-drug interactions, and therapeutic drug monitoring. Specifically, the translational pharmacology group aims to understand variability in drug toxicity, drug metabolism and drug transport. Examples of this include cell-based models such as induced-pluripotent stem cells, primary human hepatocytes, and clinical studies. The pharmacoepidemiological research group utilizes the world-class Danish registries as well as international data sources to assess pharmacological questions in large populations. The environmental medicine group studies the impact of early life exposures to environmental chemicals. In particular PFAS is a focus area, with studies of the adverse health effects of exposure, biomonitoring and advising national and international authorities. The analytical chemistry laboratory analyzes concentrations of drugs or environmental chemicals in various matrices. 

In the Environmental Medicine group we are looking for a post doc funded by Novo Nordic Foundation and ERC advanced grant. The projects focus on the Odense Child Cohort and study the impact of early life exposures to environmental chemicals. Especially PFAS and their adverse effects on maternal and child health (e.g. the brain, immune, metabolic and reproductive system). In addition, we aim to identify toxicity of short PFAS including trifluoroacetic acid, widely used but considered less toxic due to their short half-life. 

We are seeking a candidate with a PhD in medicine, pharmacology, public health, or a related discipline. Work within environmental medicine is an advance, and epidemiological and statistical skills are essential. Motivation, curiosity, and a strong drive to excel in environmental research are very important. Excellent communication skills in written and spoken English is a requirement. The position includes independent scientific writing, clinical project leading, and supervision of students. You should be interested in contributing both to the scientific armamentarium in our department and to our collegial culture. It is also expected that the post doc contributes to additional fundraising for the projects as well as research collaborations and the continuation of the Odense Child Cohort, and takes on teaching responsibilities within the department. You will, in your daily work, refer to Professor Tina Kold Jensen, but also engage in a very active collaboration with the full research group.


Your qualifications

  • PhD in medicine, pharmacology, public health, or a related discipline.

  • Experience within environmental medicine is considered an advantage

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English

  • Ability to work independently with scientific writing and publication

  • Interest in and experience with supervision of students

  • Commitment to contributing to both scientific excellence and a positive collegial culture within the department

  • Interest in establishing and maintaining national and international research collaboration
     

Further information

Interviews can be performed online if needed. If you will need to relocate to Denmark for the position, both the University and the research group will provide ample support.

Additional information about the position can be obtained from Tina Kold Jensen (tkjensen@health.sdu.dk; 0045 29464350).

title: PhD Position in Data-driven Critical Raw Material Supply Chain Resilience
description:
Do you want to investigate the resilience of critical raw material supply chains supporting low-carbon and digital technologies? Join us as a PhD student at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, University of Southern Denmark.

The Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a three-year PhD position in data-driven critical raw material supply chain resilience.

The position will be based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, Faculty of Engineering, at the SDU Odense campus. The expected starting date is 15 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

Project Overview

The deployment of low-carbon technologies, electrification and digital infrastructure is increasing global demand for critical raw materials. At the same time, the production and processing of many of these materials are geographically concentrated and exposed to geopolitical, economic, environmental and logistical disruptions.

Understanding how technology development affects material demand, in-use stocks, end-of-life flows and global supply dependencies is therefore important for assessing and strengthening the resilience of critical raw material supply chains.

The PhD position is jointly funded through research projects on critical raw material supply chains and material requirements for Denmark’s climate-neutral transition. The project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment combining environmental systems analysis, supply-chain research and data science.

 

PhD Topic Description

The PhD project will develop modular and data-driven approaches for analysing critical raw material demand, supply-chain dependencies and resilience.

A central methodological contribution will be the development of transparent, reusable and reproducible computational modules for dynamic material flow analysis. The modules will support the integration of technology deployment scenarios, material intensities, product lifetimes, stocks and flows, end-of-life management, recycling, production, trade, facility and ownership data.

The developed approaches will be applied to selected technology systems, including Denmark’s wind-energy infrastructure and the rapidly expanding infrastructure supporting data centres and AI computing. These cases will be analysed within a common methodological framework to examine how infrastructure expansion and technological change influence demand for critical and scarce materials, in-use stocks, future waste flows, recycling potential and global supply-chain dependencies.

The project may also investigate overlapping material requirements and competition for materials across low-carbon and digital technologies. Particular attention may be given to supply concentration, host–by-product dependencies, trade and ownership structures, supply bottlenecks, cascading risks and potential resilience strategies.

Depending on the candidate’s academic background and the specific research questions, the project may include network analysis, geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, uncertainty analysis, machine learning and other AI-supported approaches.

The candidate will build on selected existing models, datasets and research activities in the group and further develop scientifically robust and reusable methods that improve transparency, comparability and reproducibility in material-system research.

The exact research focus and detailed PhD plan will be developed jointly with the successful candidate, taking into account the project objectives, academic background and research interests.

In addition to a PhD dissertation and high-quality scientific publications, the project is expected to produce reusable modelling methods, documented datasets and reproducible computational workflows.

 

PhD Position and Research Environment

As a PhD student, you will conduct independent research under the supervision of an interdisciplinary team, contribute to high-quality scientific publications and participate actively in a collaborative research environment.

You will join SDU Life Cycle Engineering, where research covers industrial ecology, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, circular economy, resource systems and sustainability transitions.

The project connects expertise in engineering, data science, mathematics, business, supply-chain research and geological resources. The wider research environment includes competences in material flow analysis, critical raw material systems, data mining, network analysis, supply-chain science, finance, investment, ownership structures, geological resources and technology systems.

The position provides opportunities for collaboration across SDU faculties and with external research partners. It may also include participation in international conferences, research visits and collaboration with relevant industrial and public-sector stakeholders.

The PhD programme follows the Danish PhD framework and includes coursework, participation in active research environments, dissemination activities, and teaching or other knowledge-dissemination duties.

 

What We Expect

We are looking for a highly motivated, independent and collaborative candidate with a strong interest in critical raw materials, quantitative modelling, data-driven research and sustainability.

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree or equivalent by the time of enrolment. Relevant academic backgrounds may include engineering, industrial ecology, sustainability science, resource management, data science, computer science, applied mathematics, operations research, supply-chain management, geoinformatics, mining or geological sciences, or another relevant natural science or quantitative discipline.

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

  • A solid academic foundation in quantitative analysis, system modelling, data science or related methods. 

  • Experience with programming and data analysis, preferably using Python or a similar programming language. 

  • Experience with data handling, including data cleaning, transformation, integration and exploratory analysis. 

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

  • The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment. 

  • Good written and spoken English. 

  • A strong interest in sustainability, critical raw materials and supply-chain resilience. 

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

  • Material flow analysis, industrial ecology or material systems modelling. 

  • Network, supply-chain or geospatial analysis. 

  • Scientific computing and reproducible research workflows. 

  • Statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, optimisation, uncertainty or scenario analysis. 

  • International trade, production facility or corporate ownership data. 

  • Critical raw materials, wind energy, digital infrastructure or data centres. 

Applicants are not expected to possess expertise in all these areas. Prior experience with material flow analysis is an advantage but is not a requirement. Relevant training will be provided according to the candidate’s background and the needs of the project.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

The application must be submitted in English through the SDU online recruitment system.

Assessment of applicants will be based on the submitted application material. The application must include:

  • Curriculum Vitae. 

  • A motivated application describing the applicant’s research interests, relevant qualifications and motivation for applying. 

  • Documentation of academic qualifications, including bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and complete transcripts of grades. 

  • Official English translations of documents not issued in English or Danish. 

  • Two letters of recommendation. 

  • A list of publications and up to two examples of relevant publications, if available. 

  • The completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  • The completed TEK form for calculation of grade-point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

  • Official documentation describing the grading system of the awarding university, if the degree was not obtained in Denmark. 

  • Examples of relevant thesis work, software, code repositories or other research outputs, where available. 

  • Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step. The place of employment is in Odense, Denmark and preferred starting date is February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

 

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

The successful candidate will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering at the Department of Green Technology. The research environment conducts interdisciplinary research on the global and systemic interactions between materials, technologies, energy, the environment and society.

The Department of Green Technology is located in Odense, the main campus of the University of Southern Denmark. Odense offers an international research environment and an open Scandinavian working culture.

 

Further Information

Further information about the scientific content of the position is available from:

Wu Chen
Associate Professor
Department of Green Technology
SDU Life Cycle Engineering
University of Southern Denmark

title: Student Assistant - Data & Analytics (BluePool and Data Governance)
description:
Do you want to help shape the future of Europe’s energy system and contribute to a fully carbon‑neutral, sustainable power grid? Are you a data engineer who is curious, open‑minded, and initiative-taking — someone who enjoys working in an explorative and collaborative environment? Do you want to collaborate with engineers, application developers, and data scientists to unlock insights from the vast amounts of data behind our services? 

We are looking for a Student Assistant to support our Data & Analytics department. This is an excellent opportunity for a student who wants practical experience working with data platforms, governance processes, documentation, and operational support activities in an international and highly technical environment. 

Nordic RCC – supporting security of supply and the green energy transition 

Nordic Regional Coordination Centre (RCC) provides critical services and insights to support the national Transmission System Operators (TSOs) in Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark — to ensure the efficient operation and use of the Nordic power system and high security of power supply at any time. 

Based in Copenhagen, Nordic RCC is one of six RCCs in Europe, equally owned by the Nordic region's four electricity TSOs: Fingrid, Statnett, Svenska Kraftnät, and Energinet. 

As European power systems integrate and evolve to meet climate goals, Nordic RCC provides regional coordination, integrated services, regional insights and recommendations to the Nordic TSOs and their control centres, to support cross-border operational security 24/7.  

Join Nordic RCC, a fast-developing company determined to make a significant impact in the energy sector and to provide for a secure and efficient transition to the green, sustainable energy system. 

Right now, we are looking for a Student Assistant to join our Data & Analytics Department. 

What You Will Be Working On 

The Data and Analytics team consists of 10 employees and consultants and plays a central role in enabling data-driven decision-making across Nordic RCC. The team develops and maintains data pipelines, analytics products, BI solutions, platform services, and information services that support operational, strategic, and regulatory needs. 

As Student Assistant, you will support various initiatives across the department, with a primary focus on NRCC's analytics platform ‘BluePool’, and data governance activities. 

Examples of tasks may include: 

BluePool Support 

  • Assisting with user onboarding and access administration 

  • Maintaining onboarding guides and user documentation 

  • Supporting training sessions and workshops 

  • Gathering and tracking user feedback 

  • Assisting with testing of new BluePool functionality 

Data Governance 

  • Supporting data governance processes and documentation 

  • Maintaining data catalogues and metadata documentation 

  • Assisting with data classification and governance activities 

  • Supporting compliance and process-related initiatives 

General Department Support 

  • Coordinating meetings and workshops 

  • Maintaining team documentation and knowledge bases 

  • Preparing presentations and communication materials 

  • Supporting project coordination and follow-up activities 

  • Assisting with ad hoc analytical and administrative tasks 

Who We Are Looking For 

You are currently enrolled in a relevant university programme, for example within data science, computer science, engineering, information management, business analytics, economics, mathematics, or a similar field. 

You do not need extensive professional experience. What matters most is that you are curious, structured, and comfortable taking ownership of practical tasks — from organizing documentation and following up on details to supporting colleagues with day-to-day needs. 

We are looking for someone who: 

  • Is detail-oriented and follows tasks through carefully 

  • Enjoys turning information into clear documentation, guides, or overviews that others can use 

  • Communicates clearly in writing and verbally 

  • Can work independently while also asking for input when needed 

  • Has an interest in data, analytics, and digital platforms 

  • Is comfortable using Microsoft Office tools 

It is an advantage, but not a requirement, if you have experience with one or more relevant tools or concepts, such as Python, SQL, Power BI, enterprise architecture, data governance, or technical documentation. 

What We Offer: 

  • A flexible student position that can be adapted to your studies 

  • Exposure to large-scale data and analytics initiatives within the energy sector 

  • Experience working in an international environment with Nordic stakeholders 

  • Insight into data governance, analytics platforms, and digital transformation 

  • Opportunities to build practical skills that are highly relevant for a future career in data and analytics 

  • A friendly and collaborative team with experienced data scientists, data engineers, and analytics specialists 

Application & Security Clearance 

Please apply online in English no later than 5 November 2026. Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis. 

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.   

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system.  

Note that as part of the recruitment process, the candidate must undergo a satisfactory background check. The position is also conditioned upon a national security clearance. Both will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.  Nordic RCC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

title: OT Security Architect - Renewables, Location: Denmark , DK - Esbjerg, DK - Copenhagen
description:
Are you an experienced and motivated OT Security Architect and do you want to leave your mark on the global energy industry? If so, we want to hear from you! 
 
Your position
 
In your new position as OT Security Architect in the Renewables division, you will be a valuable member of the OT Security Team, whose mission is to ensure excellent OT security deliveries on large-scale EPC substation projects. You will have the chance to take the architectural lead and help shape a collaborative team culture built on expertise and knowledge-sharing. Above all, your work will make a real difference to the global energy sector.

Your place of work will be at one of our offices in either Esbjerg or Copenhagen. The position is full-time, and you can expect to travel 10–30 days per year.

“Every day, we help enable the green energy transition by building secure, resilient OT solutions that ensure renewable energy assets operate safely and reliably.” - OT Security Architect & Team Lead, Reza Sarafrazjoo.
 
Your tasks & responsibilities 

In our Renewables division, we have major EPC projects in the pipeline for both short- and long-term operations. As an OT Security Architect, you will take the architectural lead and support all OT Security areas across the EPC substation projects.

Your tasks will include but are not limited to:

  • Contributing to the implementation of industry-accepted good practice and required Cyber/OT Security architecture at solution level, typically based on standards such as IEC 62443, ISO 27001, and NIS
  • Helping define products and standards relevant to OT Security and infrastructure
  • Hands-on experience with cybersecurity audits and compliance frameworks, including ISO 27001, Critical Infrastructure regulations, and IEC 62443
  • Reviewing requirements/ITT packages and providing input to tenders consisting of calculations, solutions, descriptions, clarifications, and reservations
  • Taking on an advisory or active role in infrastructure, identity access management, or logging/event-based activities
  • Being responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing FAT, SAT, and SIT activities to ensure successful system delivery and integration
  • Implementing customer-specific Cyber/OT Security requirements in substation design for multiple systems and subsystems, such as SCADA, low-voltage, HVAC, Auxiliary Control and Monitoring System, etc.


Crucial to this position is your ability to take ownership of project deliverables and coordinate OT Security deadlines with internal and external stakeholders. You should thrive in a leading role where your skills, collaboration, and structured approach help ensure that requirements are met.
 
Your profile & qualifications

You are a team player who enjoys leading projects and working with stakeholders to align on timing, scope, and objectives. You know when technical expertise should be brought in to support delivery. To us, this means that you have a structured and solution-oriented approach, the ability to influence stakeholders, and the dedication to see tasks through to completion.

You will be part of a team of six colleagues that values quality, attention to detail, and a flexible working environment. We are sociable, helpful, and open to input, and we work in a dedicated, structured, and execution-focused way while respecting the agility that is a natural part of our core tasks. We want the same from you.

To succeed in this position, we imagine that you have:

  • A minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in OT Security from a similar position
  • A Tech Lead mentality – we are not seeking an extreme subject matter expert, but a well-rounded colleague who can work through heavily structured large projects involving many stakeholders 
  • The ability to know when additional technical specialists or resources are needed to complete a project
  • Excellent communication skills and fluency in English
  • Experience working in complex engineering projects, as well as project and stakeholder management, is an advantage


If you have any questions, you are more than welcome to contact OT Security Architect & Team Lead, Reza Sarafrazjoo.
 
Welcome to Semco Maritime

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey: how to get there. We provide the answers needed to make change real, because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever, pragmatic solutions. This is what we do, and this is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.
So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. 

Care to join the movement?
Change. With us.

Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.

title: Chip Ecosystem Partnership and Funding Manager, The position is a Senior Advisor at TEK Innovation
description:
Do you want to help facilitate and grow the semiconductor and chip ecosystem in Denmark and beyond, working with the leading researchers in the field, and to turn potential into opportunities, partnerships and projects? Then this job could be for you.  

About the position 

SDU Microelectronics at TEK, headed by professor Farshad Moradi, is part of the Danish Chips Competence Centre (DkCCC) - the new Danish hub for chip technology and your strategic platform. The position offers an opportunity to play a central role in strengthening Denmark’s chip ecosystem and to help connect the ecosystem with fast-growing application areas such as drones, robotics, sensors and autonomous systems, where advanced chip technology is becoming increasingly critical for performance, reliability, energy efficiency and future innovation. 

You will work closely with SDU researchers, DkCCC partners, Danish universities, companies, incubators, industry organizations, funding advisers and European chip networks. Learn more here www.dkccc.eu 

The position involves regular travel within Denmark and occasional travel elsewhere in Europe. 

Your main responsibilities will include:  

  • Identifying relevant national and European funding opportunities in chip technology, semiconductor development, and chip-enabled applications. 

  • Developing and maintaining a strategic pipeline of funding calls, project ideas and potential consortium partners. 

  • Engaging proactively with Danish start-ups, SMEs and established companies to understand their technological needs and funding requirements. 

  • Connecting companies with relevant researchers, facilities and competencies at SDU and other Danish universities. 

  • Helping companies and researchers translate technical and business ideas into fundable project concepts. 

  • Initiating and facilitating Danish and European consortia for chip-related funding calls and identifying opportunities to join existing consortia. 

  • Promoting Danish chip competencies and contribute to the visibility and strategic development of DkCCC.  

  • Supporting the full process of funding applications, from project objectives and facilitating consortiums, to coordinating proposals with partners and funding advisers. 

  • Building relationships with key stakeholders, organizing activities, and events supporting the ecosystem.   

Your profile 
You have a relevant master's degree, for example within engineering or natural sciences, business development or innovation management, economics or business administration, European studies or public policy, research and innovation management, or another relevant field. 

You have documented experience in one or more of the following: 

  • National or European research and innovation funding 

  • Development of collaborative funding proposals 

  • Consortium building and partner identification 

  • University–industry collaboration or innovation/business development 

  • Supporting start-ups, SMEs or deep-tech companies 

  • Stakeholder management and professional networking 

We are looking for a colleague who: 

  • Is proactive and comfortable initiating contact with companies, researchers and potential partners.  

  • Is a strong relationship builder who can establish trust across organizational and disciplinary boundaries 

  • Understands both commercial needs and academic interests and can structure complex consortium-development processes, while maintaining momentum towards a deadline 

  • Communicates clearly with different stakeholders, technical, academia and experts, business 

  • Works independently and is persistent and solution oriented, while also contributing actively to a team 

Experience with semiconductors, microelectronics, integrated circuits, quantum technologies, photonics, sensors or other deep-tech fields is a significant advantage — though you don't need to be a chip designer. What matters more is your ability to grasp technology-based opportunities, engage technical specialists, and turn complex ideas into fundable partnerships. Knowledge of European research and innovation programs, including EU Chips Act calls, is also an advantage. 

What we offer 

  • Become part of SDU’s growing environment for microelectronics and chip technology. 

  • Build partnerships that may lead to new products, technologies, companies, and investments. 

  • Work directly with promising Danish start-ups, companies and research environments. 

  • Help create new university–industry collaborations. 

  • Develop national and European networks within a strategically important technology area. 

  • Influence the formation of projects from their earliest stages.  

  • Collaborate with leading researchers and industry specialists, in an international and interdisciplinary environment. 

  • A role with considerable independence and the opportunity to shape the methods, networks, and activities used to identify funding opportunities and develop consortia. 

Your organizational home will be TEK Innovation, the research support and innovation unit at TEK, where you will have colleagues with similar jobs, supporting emerging ecosystems, as well as funding advisors and project managers. Your academic home with SDU Microelectronics, where you will work closely with professor Farshad Moradi and his team.  

For further information about the position, please contact: 

Thit Juul Hvid, Head of TEK Innovation, The Technical Faculty at The University of Southern Denmark tjuul@tek.sdu.dk 

Professor Farshad Moradi, SDU Microelectronics, The Technical faculty at The University of Southern Denmark at moradi@sdu.dk  

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support. 

The application deadline is November 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST).

First Interview: week 46, second interview, week 47.

The startdate will be January 1, 2027, or at the earliest convenience.

Salary and employment terms:  

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Employment shall take place in accordance with the framework agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Application must include cover letter, CV and exam certificate. All documents in connection with the application should not contain CPR number (civil registration number) – in that case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

All documents must be in English and PDF format.  All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected.  

You can only apply for the position at – https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/job-sdu. 

All attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. Cover letter and CV can contain max. 5 Mb.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark was established to create value for and with society. Whether our contributions come in the form of excellent research, innovative solutions, education or learning, we must make a positive difference to society and contribute to a sustainable future. We do this by cultivating talents and creating the best environments for research and learning. It is therefore crucial that SDU retains, develops and recruits talent. At the same time, we need to ensure consistently high quality in all our activities – and we can only do that with the right people. The University’s researchers, lecturers, students, managers and technical/administrative staff are the foundation of our success.
